The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #4b6916;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #4b6916;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4b6916;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697d;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #00697d;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697d;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #983167;">Gene Y</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #983167;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983167;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #894d00;">Gene D</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #894d00;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #894d00;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e57;">Gene F</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006e57;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e57;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4f4eb8;">Gene P</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #4f4eb8;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4f4eb8;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #785800;">Gene A</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #785800;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #785800;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #245dab;">Gene N</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #245dab;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #245dab;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #983167;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #983167;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983167;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #785800;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #785800;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #785800;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene K</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #983167;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #983167;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983167;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a32c3b;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #a32c3b;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a32c3b;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #037132;">Gene W</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #037132;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #037132;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #245dab;">Gene X</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #245dab;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #245dab;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #95411e;">Gene A</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #95411e;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #95411e;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #037132;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #037132;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #037132;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4f4eb8;">Gene R</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #4f4eb8;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4f4eb8;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #785800;">Gene A</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #785800;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #785800;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #743ab5;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #743ab5;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #743ab5;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #785800;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #785800;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #785800;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e57;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006e57;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e57;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853c88;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #853c88;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #853c88;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #785800;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e57;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006e57;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e57;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #245dab;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #245dab;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #245dab;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #4b6916;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #4b6916;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4b6916;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697d;">Gene T</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #00697d;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697d;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853c88;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #853c88;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #853c88;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #95411e;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e57;">Gene W</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006e57;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e57;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #743ab5;">Gene Y</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #743ab5;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a32c3b;">Gene B</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #a32c3b;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a32c3b;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e57;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006e57;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e57;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4f4eb8;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #4f4eb8;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4f4eb8;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a32c3b;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #656018;">Gene R</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #656018;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #656018;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #245dab;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #245dab;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #245dab;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #037132;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006592;">Gene T</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006592;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006592;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853c88;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #853c88;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #853c88;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #894d00;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #894d00;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #894d00;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e57;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006e57;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e57;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #743ab5;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #743ab5;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #743ab5;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a32c3b;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #a32c3b;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a32c3b;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4b6916;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #4b6916;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4b6916;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697d;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #00697d;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697d;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #785800;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #785800;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #785800;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene E</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853c88;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #853c88;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #853c88;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #894d00;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #894d00;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #894d00;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #037132;">Gene R</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #037132;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #037132;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4f4eb8;">Gene Y</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #4f4eb8;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4f4eb8;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #95411e;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #95411e;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #95411e;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4b6916;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #4b6916;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4b6916;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697d;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #00697d;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697d;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #785800;">Gene B</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #785800;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #785800;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697d;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #00697d;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697d;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853c88;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #853c88;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #853c88;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a32c3b;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #037132;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #037132;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #037132;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006592;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006592;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #785800;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #785800;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #785800;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697d;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #00697d;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697d;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #743ab5;">Gene Y</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #743ab5;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #743ab5;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a32c3b;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #a32c3b;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a32c3b;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e57;">Gene X</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006e57;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e57;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4f4eb8;">Gene Y</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #4f4eb8;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #95411e;">Gene N</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #95411e;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #95411e;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #037132;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #037132;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #037132;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #743ab5;">Gene X</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #743ab5;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #743ab5;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #894d00;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #894d00;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #894d00;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #037132;">Gene N</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #037132;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #037132;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853c88;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #853c88;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #853c88;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #785800;">Gene A</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #785800;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #785800;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene J</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853c88;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #853c88;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #853c88;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #95411e;">Gene B</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #95411e;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #95411e;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e57;">Gene E</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006e57;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e57;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #245dab;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #245dab;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #245dab;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #785800;">Gene N</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #785800;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #785800;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #245dab;">Gene R</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #245dab;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #245dab;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #983167;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #983167;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983167;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #037132;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #037132;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #037132;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006592;">Gene P</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006592;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006592;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #983167;">Gene W</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #983167;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983167;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #656018;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #656018;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #656018;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697d;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #00697d;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697d;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853c88;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #853c88;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #853c88;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a32c3b;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #a32c3b;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a32c3b;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene R</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4f4eb8;">Gene W</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #4f4eb8;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4f4eb8;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #95411e;">Gene J</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #95411e;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #95411e;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #037132;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #037132;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #037132;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #743ab5;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #743ab5;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #743ab5;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a32c3b;">Gene C</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #a32c3b;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a32c3b;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #656018;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #656018;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #656018;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006592;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006592;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006592;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #785800;">Gene H</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #785800;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #785800;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene N</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #983167;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #983167;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983167;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #785800;">Gene J</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #785800;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #785800;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #743ab5;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #743ab5;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #743ab5;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #894d00;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #894d00;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #894d00;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #037132;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #037132;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #037132;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853c88;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #853c88;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #853c88;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #95411e;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #95411e;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #95411e;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4b6916;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #4b6916;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4b6916;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697d;">Gene N</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #00697d;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697d;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #656018;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #656018;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #656018;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697d;">Gene N</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #00697d;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697d;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #743ab5;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #743ab5;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #743ab5;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse;
